title: LTS channel coverage and graceful upgrade plans for runtime/API/SDK/Console
creator: Aisha N. Patel
description:
Objective: define a single, pragmatic LTS channel specification that covers the runtime, public API, official SDKs, and Console UI; and deliver an automated upgrade tooling + gating blueprint that enables safe cohort rollouts with measurable rollback triggers.

Scope and goals:
- Produce a support matrix that maps: runtime binary versions, REST API surface versions, SDK minor/patch guarantees, and Console feature-flag compatibility windows.
- Define upgrade semantics across surfaces (what "compatible" means for runtime->API->SDK->Console transitions).
- Design rollout gates and telemetry that enable automated progressive rollouts (canary -> staged cohorts -> global) and deterministic rollbacks.
- Deliver a preflight validator and CI checks ("redwood-upgrade-check") that runs cross-surface compatibility tests and smoke evals before any rollout.
- Publish an operator playbook with explicit rollback choreography, timed safety windows, and a postmortem checklist.

Key principles (trade-offs and decisions):
1) Conservative compatibility: LTS channels guarantee backward-compatible runtime and API behavior for the supported window; breaking changes are only allowed on stability/release branches, not on LTS. This increases patch churn but minimizes customer-facing regressions.
2) Surface-coupling tolerance: SDKs and Console may lag runtime by up to one minor version if a compatibility adapter is provided; otherwise they require pinned compatibility. This reduces simultaneous cross-surface releases.
3) Observable SLOs first: rollouts proceed only when latency, error-rate, and model-quality regressions are under thresholds agreed in the SLO catalog. Functional regressions (e.g., structured output schema changes) are treated as P0 and block promotion.

Support matrix (high level):
- Runtime: LTS channels (e.g., runtime-2.lts) receive security/patch fixes for 18 months; critical backports allowed. Major/runtime-incompatible features land in stability channel.
- API: Semantic versioning by contract; LTS maps to a stable API minor (2.x) with deprecation windows and compatibility shims for 12 months.
- SDKs: Official SDKs adopt a "compat adapter" strategy: patch/bugfix releases backported to LTS clients; breaking SDK changes are released as vNext with clear migration guides.
- Console: Feature flags gate UI-visible changes; Console LTS offers toggle-based compatibility mode to hide new features for LTS clusters.

Rollout gates and automation:
- Preflight (CI): redwood-upgrade-check runs integration smoke tests, cross-surface contract tests, and eval-run on representative prompts. Must pass in CI before canary.
- Canary (1% traffic): Automated health checks for 15m. Gates: 99.9th percentile latency delta < 20%, error-rate < 0.1%, model-quality/regression score within threshold.
- Staged cohorts (10%, 30%, 60%): each stage has progressive time windows and stricter SLO pass thresholds. Manual approve required before global.
- Global: rolling update with automated throttling. If any cohort exceeds thresholds, rollback to prior LTS release and open a postmortem.

Telemetry and rollback triggers (conservative defaults):
- Latency: p95 increase > 30% sustained for 10 minutes -> pause.
- Errors: HTTP 5xx rate increase > 0.5% absolute or doubled baseline -> immediate rollback.
- Model quality: eval-set BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-similarity drop > threshold or increased hallucination alerts -> pause and investigate.
- Console regressions: JS bundle errors or dashboard rendering failures -> rollback console frontends via feature-flag disable.

Upgrade tooling deliverables:
- redwood-upgrade-check (CLI): cross-surface sanity validations (API contract tests, SDK method compatibility checks, model-output smoke evals, KV-cache compatibility tests).
- compatibility-report: generates per-surface compatibility scorecard and a suggested rollout plan for cohorts.
- auto-rollout-controller: controller that interfaces with deployer to automate staged traffic shifts and enforce gates.
- preflight-evals repo: canonical prompt sets and expected output signatures used during gating.

Testing and verification strategy:
- Cross-surface contract suite (PR-gated): run for every runtime change that touches API/behaviour surfaces.
- Synthetic and production shadow tests: run production-like load in a shadow environment with live traffic sampling.
- Canary evaluation harness: evaluate model outputs with deterministic scoring and human review when thresholds are near limit.

Operator playbook (summary):
- Pre-rollout: run redwood-upgrade-check, obtain canary bucket, schedule maintenance window for cohorts >30%.
- During rollout: monitor the compatibility-report and automatic telemetry channels; maintain open incident bridge.
- On trigger: run rollback script that pins routing and re-APIs SDK pin matrix, notify customers via status page if >5% impacted.
- Post-rollout: capture snapshots, run regression-eval sweep, and open follow-up engineering bugs tagged with labels: release-lab, regression, postmortem.

Docs & artifacts (links):
- PRD: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/LTS+Channel+Design+PRD
- Upgrade tool prototype (repo): https://github.com/redwood-inference/upgrade-tools/tree/lts-prototype
- Compatibility test harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/compatibility-harness
- Example rollout runbook: https://drive.google.com/example-rollout-runbook

Next steps and acceptance criteria:
- Draft formal support matrix table and publish internal confluence page (acceptance: matrix approved by Release Engineering and Product).
- Prototype redwood-upgrade-check and land minimal contract tests in CI (acceptance: CI gateable preflight step).
- Run an end-to-end dry-run (shadow traffic) upgrade for runtime-2.3.lts -> 2.4.lts on staging and capture compatibility-report (acceptance: no P0 regressions and automated cohort gating exercised).
